name: Himsa
label: Revelation
lede: Seattle hardcore kids named their metal band after the opposite of nonviolence, burned through a dozen members, turned down half the tours they were offered, and quit right after making what they called their best record.

eras.title: Ahimsa, minus the A
eras.text: Hardcore had spent a decade on Krishna-conscious nonviolence, ahimsa. A crew of Seattle scene lifers flipped the word to its opposite, himsa, harm, and aimed at Swedish-style metal instead of Youth Crew. Revelation, the label that had put out Shelter, signed them.

years.h: Himsa form in Seattle
years.p: Singer Christian "Xtian" Schmitt, guitarist Brian Johnson, bassist [[Derek Harn|882786bf-e5af-441b-b416-e46bc7ac5e1a]] and drummer Mike Green start Himsa, with guitarists Henry and Aaron Edge in the first lineup.
years.xp: The name is the Sanskrit word for harm or violence, the inverse of ahimsa, the nonviolence principle straight edge's Krishna wing had been preaching for years.

years.h: Himsa's first 7" on Revelation
years.p: A self-titled Himsa EP comes out on Revelation. The first press includes 220 on blue vinyl.

years.h: Ground Breaking Ceremony · Revelation REV 87
years.p: Himsa's debut album, cut at Raimstorm Studio with Steve Carter and Paul Speer producing. Christian Schmitt sings; it's the only Himsa full-length without John Pettibone.
years.xp: It opens on a short instrumental and then leans long: several songs run past four minutes. The LP's first press included 223 on clear vinyl.

eras.title: The singer from Undertow
eras.text: In one year Himsa went through three singers, three drummers and a keyboard player. What came out the other side was John Pettibone, the voice of Seattle straight edge band Undertow, and the lineup that would make Himsa's name.

years.h: John Pettibone of Undertow becomes Himsa's singer
years.p: After Christian Schmitt leaves and Chris LaPointe passes through, [[John Pettibone|eea60dae-22af-4e2c-89d3-ff675e97f548]] takes the mic. [[Kirby Charles Johnson|a2e52b31-705d-4ef4-9d68-83d2b15517c6]] joins on guitar and Tim Mullen settles in on drums.
years.xp: Pettibone had known Himsa's founders since the early '90s Seattle hardcore scene, from his years in Undertow and [[Nineironspitfire|d7ceabd6-7134-4ab3-9362-b87731228102]]. The 2000 turnover also brought and lost drummer John Harnett, guitarist EJ Bastien and keyboardist Clay Layton.

years.h: Death Is Infinite, John Pettibone's first Himsa record
years.p: Himsa's last release on Revelation, and the first with John Pettibone singing. The first press was 300 on green vinyl and 820 on black.

eras.title: Lamb of God makes a phone call
eras.text: Himsa moved to Prosthetic, a label barely off the ground, and grew up with it. They also got a reputation: the band that kept saying no to tours and festivals, because the D.I.Y. rules they'd learned in hardcore still applied.

q: We were stern to the D.I.Y. ethic
years.h: Lamb of God steer Himsa to Prosthetic Records
years.p: According to John Pettibone, [[Lamb of God|298909e4-ebcb-47b8-95e9-cc53b087fc65]] saw Himsa at a local show, were impressed, and connected them with Prosthetic Records.
years.xp: Prosthetic was in its early days, and Pettibone says Himsa grew with the label. The friction came later: Himsa turned down so many tours and festivals that they became, in his words, the no band, and label support shrank.

years.h: Himsa record at Robert Lang Studios, Shoreline
years.p: Himsa track Courting Tragedy and Disaster at Robert Lang Studios in Shoreline, Washington, and Orbit Audio in Seattle, with Steve Carter producing.

yt: Rain to the Sound of Panic, music video
years.h: Courting Tragedy and Disaster · Prosthetic
years.p: Swedish death metal twin leads under hardcore screaming. Brandan Schieppati of [[Bleeding Through|55fd865d-4a0d-4fd0-af19-7e6feb168ab8]] and original guitarist Aaron Edge add backing vocals.
years.xp: The lineup: John Pettibone, Kirby Charles Johnson, Sammi Curr on guitar and keys, Derek Harn and Tim Mullen. Critics lumped it with [[Darkest Hour|e0ededb4-6085-4f68-90f7-89bc560930a3]], [[Shadows Fall|2e3b75d8-00a8-486a-b4e7-a1f8f65e64c9]] and God Forbid.
play: Rain to the Sound of Panic

years.h: Chad Davis replaces Tim Mullen on Himsa's drums
years.p: Tim Mullen leaves after Courting Tragedy and Disaster and Chad Davis takes over the kit. Guitarist Matt Wicklund comes in the same year and stays until 2005.

yt: Rain to the Sound of Panic, NEMHF 2003
years.h: Himsa at the New England Metal and Hardcore Festival
years.p: Himsa play Rain to the Sound of Panic at the 2003 New England Metal and Hardcore Festival.

years.h: You've Seen Too Much: Himsa on DVD
years.p: Himsa's live and tour DVD comes out.

years.h: Seattle's Himsa record Hail Horror in Denmark
years.p: For their third album, Himsa leave the Northwest and record in Denmark, a short hop from the Swedish metal sound they'd been chasing since 1998.

eras.title: Stable at last, and done
eras.text: Himsa finally had a lineup that held, a Century Media deal and tours on three continents. Then, with the best record of their lives just out, they called it.

years.h: Hail Horror, Himsa's last album for Prosthetic
years.p: The Denmark sessions come out as Himsa's third full-length.

years.h: Himsa tour with Darkest Hour and the Acacia Strain
years.p: Himsa hit the road with [[Darkest Hour|e0ededb4-6085-4f68-90f7-89bc560930a3]], [[The Acacia Strain|08bebce9-33fa-4ae9-9992-4e5d137d655b]], A Life Once Lost and Dead to Fall.

years.h: Himsa tour Australia and sign to Century Media
years.p: Himsa tour Australia with [[Parkway Drive|a436dd02-0549-4c91-b608-df451217fdeb]] and Cry Murder, and sign with Century Media Records the same month.

years.h: Joe Frothingham replaces Chad Davis on drums
years.p: Chad Davis leaves Himsa and Joe Frothingham plays drums for the band's final year.

years.h: Summon in Thunder · Century Media
years.p: Himsa go in on April 23, 2007, at Robert Lang and Woodshed, with [[Devin Townsend|93e8c41e-8e4f-4d08-bbf5-bc1a903b2423]] producing the vocals. Videos: Unleash Carnage and Big Timber.

q: It's time to let it go.
years.h: Derek Harn announces Himsa's breakup
years.p: Bassist Derek Harn says Himsa will end after ten-plus years, four releases and constant lineup upheaval, even though the band is getting along and Summon in Thunder is their best work.
years.xp:
Harn's statement was almost cheerful: a great CD, a great label, everyone getting along, and the last three years relatively stable. After a decade of sacrifices, it was time to let it go.

Last.fm's summary puts it down to touring burnout, with John Pettibone moving to side projects and done with long tours.

years.h: Himsa's last show, at El Corazon in Seattle
years.p: Himsa play their final show at El Corazon, the Seattle club formerly called the Off Ramp. John Pettibone would later run production there.

years.h: John Pettibone starts Heiress
years.p: Four months after the last Himsa show, John Pettibone fronts the Seattle band Heiress.
years.xp: He'd already sung in The Vows and Iamthethorn. After Himsa he also tour-managed [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] and sang backups on their 2009 album Axe to Fall.

eras.title: Rehearsing as Crushpile
eras.text: Himsa came back quietly and only on their own turf: warm-up shows under fake names, then Halloween at the same club where they'd quit.

years.h: Himsa play secret warm-ups as Crushpile and Metalmucul
years.p: Himsa test the waters with practice shows under the names Crushpile and Metalmucul before admitting who they are.

years.h: Himsa's reunion show, back at El Corazon
years.p: John Pettibone, Derek Harn, Kirby Charles Johnson, Sammi Curr and Chad Davis play El Corazon on Halloween, eight years after their last show there. Reunion shows stay in the Seattle area.

years.h: Himsa at Northwest Terror Fest, Seattle
years.p: Himsa play Seattle's Northwest Terror Fest, one of the rare dates of the reunion.
